baseline_and_candidate.baseline: A0: gpt-6-astra at max effort through the frozen codex exec command, today's default for every GPT-6 step.
baseline_and_candidate.candidate: A1 (gpt-6-astra, medium), S0 (gpt-6-sol, max), S1 (gpt-6-sol, medium), L0 (gpt-6-luna, max) and L1 (gpt-6-luna, medium). Each arm runs the same 25 batches of the same 360 filings, with the same prompt, schema and command.

predeclared_metrics.quality_rule: An arm is routable for mechanical 8-K item extraction when (1) the paired bootstrap (10,000 resamples, seed 20260926) 95% lower bound of micro-F1(arm) - micro-F1(A0) is at least -0.02, (2) its JSON-valid rate is at least 0.98, and (3) every one of its batches completed. Among routable arms whose every call reported usage, the recommendation is the arm with the lowest mean billed tokens per filing; ties go to the lower median wall time of ok calls, then to plan order. A0 is itself a candidate. Micro-F1 is over per-accession item-code sets against the filer-declared header ITEMS, with li26's scoring functions; macro-F1, exact match, per-filing precision and recall, failures and wall time are reported alongside.
predeclared_metrics.usage_rule: Record Codex turn.completed usage for every call, including failed, retried, limit and interrupted calls: input, cached input, cache-write input, output (which includes reasoning) and reasoning. Billed tokens per filing = (input - cached input + output) / 360. Cached input and reasoning are reported separately, and reasoning is never added to output a second time. A call without usage (other than one ended by the usage limit) leaves its arm unranked. Quota percentages are context only. No whole-task savings claim.

runtime_and_platform.platform: nativestack-5975wx-20260925: WSL2 Ubuntu 24.04.5 x86_64. Hosted GPT-6 models are reached through the native Codex sign-in.

tools.name: Python
tools.version: 3.11 or newer standard library for run_arm.py and analyze.py

runtime_and_platform.isolation: Each call runs codex exec with --ignore-user-config, a read-only sandbox, stdin /dev/null and no --search, from an empty 0700 directory outside every repository, with RUST_LOG removed. At most three calls run at once, and every call holds one of the host's three Codex slot locks. Replies, events and records stay in a private 0700 state directory. This is not an OS sandbox around codex itself.

commands: uv run --no-project --with jsonschema --with pyyaml python -B -m unittest tests.test_gpt6_family_tiering_20260926 -v
limitations: Preregistration only: no arm ran and no provider call was made for this record.
One task on one day: 360 filings of 2020-03-02 in 25 batches. A routing result covers mechanical extraction with a deterministic scorer, not general quality.
Labels are filer-declared header ITEMS, not hand-checked or frontier-model labels; li26's 16,000-character input cap applies to every arm alike.
One run per arm. Codex exec exposes no temperature or seed, so the bootstrap covers filing sampling, not run-to-run variation; provider behaviour and models may change after the run.
Batches of up to 15 filings share one prompt and one reply, so the result holds for this batching, not for single-filing or larger batches.
Each call also carries Codex's own instructions and tool definitions, which are part of every arm's measured tokens; the prompt tells the model to use no tool, and any tool use counts in its arm.

Under --ignore-user-config, gpt-6-sol and gpt-6-luna run at their catalog default priority tier and gpt-6-astra at its default. Wall time is a shared-host, shared-account observation and only breaks ties.
Quota percentages cannot be attributed to one arm, because other sessions share the account; they are context only.
The six arms spend a few million tokens of the shared allowance, and a usage limit can stop an arm until the reset.

decision_and_scope.scope: Frozen paired comparison of A1, S0, S1, L0 and L1 against A0 (gpt-6-astra at max effort) for batched 8-K item extraction on the 2020-03-02 cohort, through codex-cli 0.157.1 on nativestack-5975wx-20260925. A routing result applies only to mechanical extraction stages with a deterministic scorer.

rollback: Nothing changes until an observed decision recommends an arm. A later routing change names the recommended model and effort in each mechanical extraction stage's own command. Rollback restores -m gpt-6-astra -c model_reasoning_effort="max" there. The experiment writes only its private state directory, which can be removed once its aggregates are recorded.
next_decision_changing_test: Run the six arms under the frozen command, resuming any limit-stopped arm after the reset, then apply analyze.py. A route_mechanical_extraction outcome qualifies only that model and effort, for mechanical extraction stages with a deterministic scorer. A different task, day, batch size or Codex version needs its own plan.
